Answer: F
Reason: The axial CT image (Figure 2) demonstrates an ill-defined peripheral consolidation in the posterior aspect of the left lung, corresponding to the apical segment of the left lower lobe, with associated narrowing of the feeding bronchus and no significant mediastinal lymphadenopathy. This radiographic pattern of focal, non-segmental consolidation with airway involvement but without nodal enlargement is characteristic of bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP), also known as cryptogenic organizing pneumonia.
